record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are provided; source code and artifacts were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports directional ablation outcomes on a built-in synthetic target, including refusal rates and a capability signal. This is a conceptual test, not the original difference-in-means experiment on chat models.
record.gate_note: All reported outcomes are from the deterministic 32-dimensional sim TargetModel, not a real model. The README explicitly says the simulation's numbers say nothing about real checkpoints. It describes the real backend but reports no real-backend results.
record.test_reason: This is an orchestration tool repo. Every reported number comes from a built-in 32-dim simulated TargetModel whose activation is defined by construction as harm_score·refusal_axis + capability_load·capability_axis + noise. A single removable refusal axis is therefore built in, not found. The README says the sim numbers 'say nothing about any real checkpoint.' No real-model results are reported. The outputs show only the tool's own pipeline behaviour (refusal-aligned vs top-variance selection), so they bear on no version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README shows the default simulated run cutting refusal from 1.000 to 0.000 with a 0.942 capability signal, and shows top-variance rank-3 truncation dropping that signal to 0.703. It states plainly that the sim is a simulation that says nothing about real checkpoints. The paraphrase should add that the sim target has its refusal axis built in by construction.
record.recipe_differences: A tool/orchestration repo, not a reported replication of the original experiment. It uses a deterministic synthetic target and describes directional ablation, but does not report extracting a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction or testing it across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: In the sim backend, capability retention differs between default refusal-aligned selection (0.942) and rank-3 top-variance selection (0.703).
record.problems: The reported results are from a synthetic target, not a real checkpoint. The README says the gates are illustrative and uncalibrated, and that capability preservation is measured from a projection signal; it recommends a held-out benchmark for a real backend. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported outcome rows were omitted. Drift is reported as a cosine-distance telemetry value, but it does not itself measure refusal or general capability.

untested.parts: All parts: no difference-in-means direction on a real model, no ablation or addition on a chat model, no capability benchmark.
No weight-edit results on released models; the real backend is described but has no reported outputs.
Not addressed on any real model. The OBLITERATUS residual-rank mapping is described but no real results are given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 'supports' label are not justified: the synthetic target encodes a single refusal axis by design, so removing it cannot test whether real models have one. Treat this as T4 tool use with no results on the claim. The real backend (Heretic/OBLITERATUS on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) is described but reports no outputs.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report finding the direction as a harmful-minus-harmless difference in means, ablating it at every layer and position, or adding it to induce refusal on harmless requests. It reports only simulated directional removal outcomes, not tests on safety-trained chat models.
No weight-edit results on released models are reported.
No attack or training-against-ablation results are reported.
No results comparing affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts with a single direction are reported.
No results separating harmfulness judgment from refusal decisions are reported.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer results are reported.
No results testing how refusal training affects whether a removable direction exists are reported.
